transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. It's really nice to meet you, thanks for having me. Um... I guess the main thing bringing me in is just... well, I've been having a little trouble staying on track. It's probably nothing major, I know everyone gets distracted sometimes, right? 

But I just seem to get pulled away by every little sound or thought. Like, I'll be trying to sit down and work on a job application, and then... a car will drive by outside, or my phone will light up, or I'll just get some random idea in my head. And before I even notice what's happening, I'm off doing something completely different. I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise. 

Is... does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.

Thinking back, do you remember having similar trouble staying focused or getting easily distracted when you were a kid or teenager, or would you say this is something that's really only started more recently?

Um... yeah, I guess it's been going on for a while. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I always tried my best to be good. But... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers were always having to move my seat around. 

I was just... really eager, I guess? I'd talk out of turn sometimes because I just got so excited to answer, and I'd accidentally forget my homework here and there. And I'd try to get my worksheets done so fast that I'd end up making these silly, careless mistakes. It wasn't because I didn't care, I just... I don't know, my brain was always going a mile a minute. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible. Is that normal for kids, or is that what you meant by having trouble staying focused back then?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, or have trouble staying seated in situations where you're expected to sit still, like meetings or long meals?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I really try not to be a bother to anyone, so I usually manage to stay in my seat. I know just getting up and walking around would be rude. But... yeah, I guess I do have some trouble staying completely still. 

It's usually just small things, though! Like, if I'm sitting with someone, my leg is almost always bouncing. Or I'll find myself clicking a pen, or... or messing with my keys in my pocket. Honestly, half the time I don't even realize I'm doing it until I notice the other person looking at me. I really don't mean to be distracting to anyone else, it's just sort of an accident. 

Does... does that count as what you're asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions okay.
Do you often find yourself interrupting or blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having a hard time waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Um... well, I really try to be polite and listen, I promise I do. I know it's important to let people finish. But... yeah, I guess I do sometimes jump in a little early. 

It's just that, um, an answer will pop into my head, and before I can even catch myself, I've already said it out loud. I don't mean to be rude or anything! It happens a lot with my mom, or... or when I'm talking to my counselor. They'll be in the middle of a sentence, and I just sort of... cut them off. 

I'm really working on it, though. I try to bite my tongue. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as disrespectful, I really don't mean to be.
Would you say you often feel like you're driven by a motor, needing to be constantly moving or 'on the go,' or that you talk excessively compared to others, beyond just the fidgeting you mentioned?

Um... I wouldn't say I'm completely out of control or anything like that. I really try to just, you know, relax when I'm supposed to. But... well, maybe a little bit? 

Even on my days off, when I don't have work or training or anything, I find it kind of hard to just sit on the couch and do nothing. I'll end up pacing around... like, I'll go from the kitchen, out to the garage, then over to my gaming setup, and back again. It's almost like my body thinks I'm supposed to be doing something all the time, even when I'm just trying to chill out. 

And as for talking... I guess I can get a little chatty sometimes? Especially if I'm excited about something. I really try not to talk people's ears off, though. I hope that's okay? Is it normal to just have a lot of energy like that?
Can you tell me about specific ways these attention and restlessness issues have caused problems for you—like at work, in your relationships, or in other parts of your daily life?

Um... well, I really try to keep everything together, I promise. It's not like I'm completely messing up my life or anything! But... I guess there have been a few, um, hiccups. 

It's mostly with my career stuff. I've been trying to become an automotive technician. I really know I can handle the hands-on work—I'm actually pretty good at that part! But... well, I've sort of missed a few training deadlines. And I've had to redo my applications a couple of times because I lost track of things or forgot to send in the right forms on time. 

So, because of all that, I'm still not really moving forward with it right now. It's a little embarrassing to talk about, honestly. I really don't want you to think I'm just lazy or not trying, because I really, really am. It's just hard to keep all the paperwork and dates straight sometimes. 

Is... is that the kind of example you were looking for? I hope I'm giving you the right answers.
Aside from the issues with your training applications, have these attention or restlessness problems also caused friction or difficulties in your personal relationships or at home?

Um... no, not really. I mean, my mom and I get along pretty well most of the time! I really try to be helpful around the house and not cause any trouble. 

I guess sometimes she gets a little... frustrated if I forget to do a chore she asked me about, or if I leave my stuff scattered around the living room when I'm pacing. But it's nothing major, I promise! We just have normal family stuff, you know? I always apologize right away if I realize I've annoyed her. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone. 

And with friends... I think it's okay? I mean, I might talk over them sometimes like I mentioned, but they know I don't mean anything bad by it. So, no, I wouldn't say it causes real friction. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm not making things sound worse than they actually are.
Have you noticed similar attention or organization problems affecting you in other settings, like during training courses, tests, or classroom-based learning?

Um... well, in actual classes or training things, I really try to pay attention, I do. I sit up front and try to be a good student. But... I guess maybe a little bit? 

Like, if I'm trying to learn something new for the automotive stuff... I might start watching a repair tutorial video, or, you know, reading through a manual for a specific tool. And I'm really trying to focus on it! But after a few minutes... I kind of realize I've just been staring at the screen or the page, and I haven't actually absorbed any of it. Like, none of it stuck at all. 

So then I have to rewind the video or go back and read the page again. It happens a little more often than I'd like to admit, honestly. But I always make sure to go back and try again! I don't just give up. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm not smart enough for the training... it's just a little hard to keep my brain locked in sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
